Getting started

Must-see places in Clermont-Fd

The 17 sights every visitor to Clermont-Ferrand should know, plus 6 extras. Tap “Show on map” to find a place, or “Directions” to get there from where you are.

City centre 10

Easy to explore on foot

Place de Jaude

The city’s main square, lined with shops and cafés. Look for the bronze statue of Vercingétorix, the Gallic chief, by Bartholdi, the sculptor of the Statue of Liberty.

Show on map Directions

Notre-Dame-de-l’Assomption Cathedral

A Gothic cathedral built from dark Volvic lava stone. Work began in 1248; its two spires were only completed in the 19th century by Viollet-le-Duc.

Show on map Directions

Notre-Dame-du-Port Basilica

A 12th-century Romanesque basilica in pale stone, listed by UNESCO as part of the Routes of Santiago de Compostela. Go down to the crypt.

Show on map Directions

Les Salins flea market

A huge flea market every Sunday morning, 7 am to 1 pm, on the Place Gambetta car park in the Salins district. Free entry; come early for the best finds.

Show on map Directions

Jardin Lecoq

An English-style garden right in the centre, with a pond, a rose garden and tall old trees. The ideal break between two visits.

Show on map Directions

FRAC Auvergne

The regional contemporary art collection, with a strong focus on painting. Exhibitions change through the year, a few steps from the cathedral.

Show on map Directions

Taste the local food

Try truffade, aligot and Auvergne cheeses such as Saint-Nectaire. The Halle gourmande Saint-Pierre, the covered market in the city centre, is a good place to start.

Show on map Directions

Tourist office, Place de la Victoire Extra

Free maps, guided tours and up-to-date opening times, right beside the cathedral.

Show on map Directions

Henri-Lecoq Natural History Museum Extra

Next to the Jardin Lecoq: rocks and volcanoes, fossils, plants and the wildlife of Auvergne.

Show on map Directions

Bargoin Museum Extra

Archaeology from Gallo-Roman Clermont, alongside a collection of textile art from around the world.

Show on map Directions

Montferrand 4

Tram A from the centre

The old historic quarter of Clermont-Ferrand. Montferrand began as a separate town, founded around 1120 by the Counts of Auvergne as a “new town” to rival Clermont, the bishops’ city next door. In the late 12th century, it was one of the first towns in the region to receive a charter giving its inhabitants rights and freedoms, including the right to run their own affairs.

King Louis XIII ordered the two towns to unite in 1630 (Edict of Troyes), and Louis XV made the union effective in 1731, which gave the city its double name. Its streets still hold Gothic and Renaissance mansions, and it was one of the first protected historic districts in France.

Medieval Montferrand

Stroll through the medieval street plan, past Gothic and Renaissance mansions with carved façades. Do not miss the Maison de l’Éléphant.

Show on map Directions

Roger-Quilliot Art Museum (MARQ)

The city’s fine-arts museum, set in a former convent in Montferrand: painting and sculpture from the Middle Ages to the 20th century, including some very large canvases.

Show on map Directions

L’Aventure Michelin

An interactive museum about Michelin, founded in Clermont in 1889: tyres, travel maps, the famous guides and the Michelin Man.

Show on map Directions

ASM Experience Extra

The museum of ASM Clermont Auvergne, the city’s rugby club, next to the Marcel-Michelin stadium.

Show on map Directions

Around the city 5

Bus, car or a good walk

Montjuzet Park

Clermont’s largest park, on a hill north of the centre: terraced gardens, a small Mediterranean garden and wide views over the city and the volcanoes.

Show on map Directions

Pierre Carrée viewpoint

The spot where locals come to see the whole of Clermont spread out below, with the cathedral at its heart. Beautiful at sunset and at night.

Show on map Directions

Wellness in Royat

Royat, the spa town next door, has been known for its springs since Roman times. Its Royatonic centre offers thermal pools, saunas and hammams.

Show on map Directions

SENSAS, an unusual experience

A team game built around your senses: touch, hearing and smell are put to the test in a series of challenges. Fun with friends; book ahead.

Show on map Directions

Les Côtes de Clermont Extra

Take the time to discover the Côtes de Clermont, a charming walk offering a splendid panoramic view over the city, its surroundings and the Chaîne des Puys.

Show on map Directions

Volcanoes & countryside 4

Car, or seasonal shuttle

Puy de Dôme summit

At 1,465 m, the highest volcano of the Chaîne des Puys, a UNESCO World Heritage site. Take the Panoramique des Dômes rack train (about 15 minutes) or hike up; at the top, views over the volcanoes and a Roman temple of Mercury.

Show on map Directions

Puy de Pariou

A textbook volcano with an almost perfectly round crater. A loop of about 6 km starts from the Goules car park in Orcines. Stay on the marked paths: the crater floor is off-limits.

Show on map Directions

Vulcania

A science park about volcanoes and planet Earth, about 15 km from Clermont: immersive films, attractions and a planetarium. Open from late March to early November.

Show on map Directions

Gergovie plateau Extra

Where Vercingétorix defeated Julius Caesar in 52 BC. A museum tells the story; the plateau offers walks and wide views. About 15 minutes south by car.

Show on map Directions

Getting started

Health insurance

As a language assistant, you are covered by health insurance managed by the French Sécurité sociale.

Registering with the Sécurité sociale

Your school’s office registers you with the CPAM de Paris (the Paris health insurance fund), whichever academy you are assigned to.

Registration with the CPAM is compulsory, even if you already have insurance in your home country.

Returning assistants who already have a social security number must send their application by post.

Choose a GP (médecin traitant)

Choosing a médecin traitant means you are better reimbursed.

When you contact a doctor for the first time to make them your GP, say that you are a foreign language assistant under contract from October to April. This will make it easier to find a GP.

Consultation fee26,50 €
Reimbursed if you have a GP18,55 €
Reimbursed if you have no GP7,95 €

You must make this choice at your first visit to the doctor, or after it. The doctor will fill in a form.

Visa validation

For language assistants from outside the European Union.

Validate your VLS-TS

As soon as you have a permanent address in France, and within 3 months of your arrival, you must validate your VLS-TS on the online portal.

  1. You will then receive an email with your username and a password.
  2. From your account, you can download your visa validation certificate.
  3. This certificate proves that your visa has been validated: be sure to keep it.

Getting started

Where to live

Finding a home is often the first challenge. The academy does not provide housing, but here are the best options and the help you are entitled to.

Housing in your school

Some schools in the academy have rooms or small flats for assistants. It is often the simplest and cheapest option. Ask your school as soon as you receive your appointment letter.

  • Check whether it stays open during the school holidays and at weekends.
  • Ask about the building’s opening hours.
  • If you come as a couple or with your family, this type of housing is not guaranteed.

Residences for young people

Young workers’ hostels (Habitat Jeunes residences) welcome working people aged 16 to 30. Rooms are furnished, the rent often includes charges and you can get housing benefit from the CAF. There are several in Clermont-Ferrand and in the other towns of the academy.

Habitat JeunesYoung workers’ hostels, from 16 to 30habitatjeunes.org LokavizThe Crous ads platform: you must be a student to contact the landlordslokaviz.fr

Flatshares and ads

Sharing a flat lowers the rent and helps you meet people. The lease can be shared by all flatmates or individual: read it carefully before signing.

Flatshare rooms near tram and busRooms in Clermont-Ferrand from 470 € a month, all charges included La Carte des ColocsFlatshares in Clermont-Ferrandlacartedescolocs.com Beelive ColivingNetwork of furnished coliving homes in Clermont-Ferrandbeelivecoliving.com Le Bon CoinRental ads in Auvergne, up to 400 € a monthleboncoin.fr SeLogerRental ads all over Franceseloger.com

Beware of scams

Never pay any money before visiting the place (or doing a video visit) and signing a lease.

Short-term rentals such as Airbnb do not give you proof of address, which you need to open a bank account.

Getting started

Housing benefit (APL)

Personalised housing aid paid by the Caisse d’allocations familiales (CAF).

Apply as soon as you move in

It is neither automatic nor backdated: apply to the CAF as soon as you move in.

This aid depends on the accommodation you live in: it must be eligible for the APL, so make sure you check this. If you are housed in a school, you will not be eligible for this aid.

As a tenant, you may be entitled to housing benefit (APL or ALS) paid by the CAF.

The aid is paid from the month after your application. Processing takes about a month if your file is complete.

Apply on caf.frInformation on Service Public

Usual documents

  • Passport or residence permit (validated VLS-TS visa for non-EU assistants)
  • Lease or rent certificate
  • French bank details (RIB)
  • Appointment letter or payslip

When you leave

Tell the CAF when you leave France at the end of your contract.

Getting started

Guarantor, insurance and check-in

Three things to sort out when you sign a lease, and where to get free advice.

Visale guarantee

In France, landlords almost always ask for a guarantor who will pay if you don’t. If you don’t have one, Action Logement’s Visale guarantee plays this role for free. It is open to all tenants aged 30 and under, whatever their job.

Apply online before signing the lease: you get a visa to show the landlord, usually within a few days.

Apply for Visale

Home insurance

Home insurance is compulsory for tenants. It must at least cover fire, explosion and water damage. Give the certificate to your landlord on the day you get the keys.

Choose a “multi-risk” policy if you can: it includes third-party liability, which also covers you outside your home. Your bank can offer you one when you open your account.

Read more on Service Public

Check-in and check-out inventory

When you move in and when you move out, you walk round the place with the landlord and note the condition of each room (état des lieux). This document decides whether you get your whole deposit back.

  • Take dated photos of each room on the day you move in.
  • You have 10 days after the check-in inventory to report a defect you missed.
  • The deposit must be returned within 1 month if the check-out inventory matches the check-in one, 2 months otherwise. Give the landlord your RIB and your future address.
Check-in inventoryCheck-out inventoryDeposit

Getting started

Before you leave

Birth certificate with parentage

A compulsory document

Before leaving your home country, you MUST have a birth certificate with parentage drawn up.

You will need it to register with French health insurance (CPAM de Paris). Here is what it must look like.

Legalisation or apostille

  • You have a multilingual birth extract: it does not need to be legalised or to bear an apostille.
  • You have no multilingual extract, and the country where your certificate was issued has signed the Hague Convention of 5 October 1961: your certificate must bear an apostille.
  • You have no multilingual extract, and that country has not signed the Hague Convention: your certificate must be legalised.

Civil status documents issued by embassies and consulates do not need an apostille or legalisation. They must state the register they were drawn up from (certificate reference, volume, page, number, etc.).

Validity

Your birth certificate must be less than one year old when you register with the CPAM de Paris. Two exceptions:

  • Certificates issued in some programme countries are valid for life*.
  • A certificate more than a year old is accepted if its apostille or legalisation is less than a year old: the date of the apostille or legalisation is what counts.

*South Africa, Australia, the Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, Belarus, Canada, Eswatini, the United States, the Gambia, Ghana, Guyana, India, Iraq, Ireland, Israel, Jamaica, Jordan, Kazakhstan, Kenya, Lesotho, Malawi, Malta, Nigeria, New Zealand, Uganda, Uzbekistan, the OECS countries, the United Kingdom, Russia, Sri Lanka, Tanzania, Trinidad and Tobago, Zimbabwe.

Content of the certificate

The certificate must show parentage: the surnames AND first names of both parents.

Your surnames and first names must be identical to those on your passport or identity card. If they differ, you must provide proof: a marriage certificate or an official change-of-name document.

If you were born in one country but hold the passport or identity card of another, a naturalisation certificate may be requested.

Translations

No translation is needed if your certificate is written in French or in one of these languages: Albanian, Croatian, Czech, Danish, Dutch, English, Finnish, German, Hungarian, Italian, Latvian, Lithuanian, Norwegian, Polish, Portuguese, Romanian, Slovak, Spanish, Swedish, Turkish.

In any other language, you can hand in your certificate without a translation: the CPAM may ask for a sworn translation later. If you already have a sworn translation of your birth certificate, send it straight away.

If you need a translation, only these are accepted:

  • a translator or interpreter listed by a French court (Tribunal de grande instance, Court of Appeal or Court of Cassation);
  • the French embassy or consulate in the country where the certificate was issued;
  • the embassy or consulate in France of the country where the certificate was issued.

Good to know

  • Your documents must be clear and legible, and must not be highlighted.
  • Your surname and first name must be identical on all your documents.

Source: Le guide de l’assistant de langue en France 2026-2027, France Éducation international.

      Getting started

      Create your ENSAP account

      ENSAP is the State's secure website where you will find your payslips. Here is how to create your account, step by step.

      Before you start

      You can only create your account once you have your own 15-digit social security number.

      Have these ready:

      • your social security number (15 digits)
      • the bank details (RIB / IBAN) of the account where your salary is paid
      • an email address you check often and your phone number

      Go to ensap.gouv.fr

      Click “Créer mon espace”. If you already have an ameli.fr or impots.gouv.fr account, you can also use the FranceConnect button.

      Open ensap.gouv.fr

      Fill in the form

      1. Identity: enter your social security number, check your name and date of birth, then complete the missing digits of your IBAN.
      2. Password: if the site asks for one, choose a strong password (at least 8 characters, with capital letters, small letters, numbers and a special character).
      3. Contact details: give your email address and your phone number.

      Activate your account within 24 hours

      You receive an email with an activation link. Click it within 24 hours. After that, the link expires and you must start again.

      No email? Check your spam folder.

      Find your payslips

      Log in to ensap.gouv.fr: your payslips are in the “Rémunération” section. Download each one as a PDF and keep it: you will be asked for it by the CAF and for other paperwork.

      Getting started

      Open a bank account

      One of the very first steps when you arrive in France.

      Do it as soon as you arrive

      Opening a bank account is one of the first things to do when you arrive in France: it is part of the first administrative steps, which need to be done very quickly.

      Choose a bank and bring these documents

      • Passport, or identity card for EU nationals
      • Your appointment letter (arrêté d’affectation)
      • Proof of address*: rent receipt, electricity bill or a letter from your landlord

      *If you do not have a permanent address yet, you can give the address of your school.

      Ask for your RIB

      Ask to receive your bank details (RIB, relevé d’identité bancaire) as soon as possible.

      This document must be provided as a PDF to the administration.

      Traditional bank or online bank?

      Since online banks appeared, many assistants seem to prefer this type of service.

      Find a bank near me

      Who can help you?

      Your mentor teacher will be able to give you all the information you need.
